=== A METHODOLOGICAL DEFECT IN MY OWN DISPATCH INSTRUCTIONS, WORTH RECORDING ===
My routine's step 4 tells me to skip any PR whose reviews/<pr>/ already holds a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA. That test is WRONG, and wrong in the direction that generates work. scripts/lwb_lanes.py compares reviewed_commit against resolve_reviewable_head(), which deliberately SKIPS commits touching only reviews/ and proof/. A record-only commit therefore advances the raw head while leaving the reviewable head -- and the record -- perfectly valid. Measured across all 18 open PRs this run: 0 of 18 had a record naming the raw head, but 16 of 18 had a valid record naming the REVIEWABLE head. Had I followed step 4 literally I would have re-reviewed 16 already-reviewed PRs, and each record-only commit I pushed would have re-advanced the raw head, making the routine a perpetual-motion churn machine that never converges. Only #53 and #63 genuinely lacked a current record. Recommend step 4 be rewritten to compare against resolve_reviewable_head().

=== FINDING 1 (re-verified, first raised by the prior reviewer at 507d659 -- STILL STANDS, unchanged code) ===
evaluate() gates on repo facts it never consumes, making the rule wholly inert wherever facts are not gathered. Verified independently by introspecting the real module rather than by reading the prior record: the ONLY references to repo inside evaluate() are `repo = event.repo`, `if repo is None:` and `if repo.facts_incomplete:`. Classification reads event.tool_input; authorisation reads config.options. The rule needs NOTHING from RepoFacts to reach its verdict, yet returns None -- silently -- when facts are absent or incomplete, at deny as well as warn. The docstring justifies this as "mirroring lwb_proof_required's discipline exactly," but that rule genuinely needs facts (it must look for a proof record, so absent facts really do mean "could not check"); this one does not. Refusing to invent an opinion you cannot have is a virtue; suppressing one you are fully able to form is not the same thing. NOT BLOCKING at the "warn" mode core/policy/default.json actually ships, but it is the fail-open shape build-plan item 1.2 exists to remove and must be resolved before the deny-arming item.

=== FINDING 2 (re-verified, first raised at 507d659 -- STILL STANDS, unchanged code) ===
The classifier OVER-matches, against its own docstring's explicit "UNDER-match, deliberately" bias. Re-measured directly against the real module this run:
    git rebase --abort     -> history_rewrite   (this UNDOES a rewrite; it is the recovery command)
    git rebase --continue  -> history_rewrite
    git rebase --skip      -> history_rewrite
    git reset --hard       -> history_rewrite   (rewrites nothing; moves HEAD nowhere)
    git reset --hard HEAD  -> history_rewrite   (likewise)
The implementation matches `sub == "rebase"` with no look at the operation flag, and `"--hard" in tokens[2:]` with no look at the target -- the "reads one field, ignores the sibling that changes its meaning" shape. The docstring's blind-spot list is under-match only and does not disclose this; the only committed test is `git reset --hard HEAD~1`, which is a genuine history discard. Armed to deny, this would block `git rebase --abort` and trap someone mid-rebase with the gate forbidding the way out. NOT BLOCKING at warn -- surfacing this is what a warn period is for -- but fix before arming: exclude --abort/--continue/--skip, and require reset --hard to name a target other than HEAD.
I independently confirmed the correct-and-silent side too: `git merge origin/main` and `gh pr merge 53 --squash` are silent (D19's carve-out holds), `echo "git push --force"` is silent (quote-blanking works, no false positive), and the two documented blind spots (`git -C /tmp push --force`, `gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/b`) behave exactly as the docstring says they do.
